statement: Let \(p\) be a prime number and \(r\) the remainder of the division of \(p\) by 210. It is known that \(r\) is a composite number and can be written as the sum of two non-zero perfect squares. Find all primes less than 2018 that satisfy these conditions.

There are \(n\) knights numbered 1 to \(n\) and a round table with \(n\) chairs. The first knight chooses his chair, and from him, knight number \(k+1\) sits \(k\) places to the right of knight number \(k\), for all \(1 \leq k \leq n-1\) (occupied and empty seats are both counted). In particular, the second knight sits next to the first. Find all values of \(n\) such that all \(n\) knights occupy all \(n\) chairs following this procedure.

You have a \(7 \times 7\) board divided into 49 unit squares. Mateo places a coin in one square.

a) Prove that Mateo can place the coin so that it is impossible for Emi to completely cover the remaining 48 squares, without gaps or overlaps, using fifteen \(3 \times 1\) rectangles and one L-tromino (a shape covering 3 squares arranged in an L, as shown in the figure).

b) Prove that no matter which square Mateo places the coin in, Emi can always cover the 48 remaining squares using fourteen \(3 \times 1\) rectangles and two L-trominos.
figure_description: Two tile shapes are shown: a 3×1 rectangle (three unit squares in a row) and an L-tromino (three unit squares arranged in an L-shape).

statement: There is a \(50 \times 50\) grid board. Carlos writes a number in each cell by the following procedure: he first chooses 100 distinct numbers \(f_1, f_2, f_3, \ldots, f_{50}, c_1, c_2, c_3, \ldots, c_{50}\), among which exactly 50 are rational. He then writes in cell \((i, j)\) the number \(f_i \cdot c_j\) (the product of \(f_i\) and \(c_j\)). Determine the maximum number of rational numbers that the cells of the board can contain.

In the plane there are 2018 points, no three of which are collinear. These points are colored with 30 colors so that no two colors have the same number of points. All triangles with three vertices of different colors are formed. Determine the number of points of each of the 30 colors so that the total number of triangles with vertices of three different colors is as large as possible.

Let \(ABCD\) be a parallelogram. An interior circle of \(ABCD\) is tangent to lines \(AB\) and \(AD\) and intersects diagonal \(BD\) at points \(E\) and \(F\). Prove that there exists a circle passing through \(E\) and \(F\) that is tangent to lines \(CB\) and \(CD\).
